ideas.title: Wind the field coil yourself
ideas.goal: The player takes the black lodestones out of the drum motor and winds copper wire round a soft-iron horseshoe instead, choosing how many turns: few turns and the field is weak and the cart crawls; many turns and it pulls hard but the long thin copper drops the voltage and the coil warms; too many and the iron saturates, so extra turns buy nothing. Every winding is an experiment the cart answers on the planks, and getting the most out of six clay pots becomes a craft you get good at.
ideas.toward: The human's s172 order puts 'iron stator motor' FIRST, and the road step 'an iron-cored wound stator (electromagnet): the motor gets strong enough for a wheel' is still open. The cart's motor gets a field it makes itself instead of lodestone, so it can be strengthened for the dune.
ideas.idea: The field comes from the existing nonlinear 2-D magnetostatic FEM (physics/motor2d.jl, Newton on a saturating B-H curve) with the coil's ampere-turns as its source, not a table: N turns of a chosen wire give the coil's resistance from length and gauge, the current from the pots' circuit, the gap flux from the solved field, and the torque and back-EMF the cart drives with. A shunt or series winding is a real choice of how the wires touch. Someone watching sees Lumi's hands wind real turns of copper onto grey iron, then the cart pull off harder than before.
ideas.form: A change to the drum motor and the cart (a coil you wind in Jump in by holding a key per layer), the field solved from the winding; a path traced film of the winding and the stronger run.

ideas.title: Crank against the load you chose
ideas.goal: The player puts a hand on the motor's crank and pushes with a force, not a speed: what the motor is wired to decides how hard it fights back. Into nothing it spins free; into the six pots it charges them and turns heavy; shorted, it nearly locks. The player feels Lenz's law in the crank, learns which load is worth the effort, and refills the pots the cart drained.
ideas.toward: The motor run backwards as a generator (road step), charging the cart's own pots by motion: the first time the cart's store is refilled, which is the regen the dune descent and the windmill both need. It measures what a hand (about 50 W) gets through the stator.
ideas.idea: Torque balance on the crank: hand torque minus k*I minus friction drives the rotor's inertia; I comes from the circuit solver (back-EMF k*omega against the pots' EMF and internal resistance, or a short), so the pots' state of charge really rises (copper plates back on). No glowing-wire show: the evidence is the crank slowing under load and the pots' blue coming back. Someone watching sees Lumi leaning into a crank that suddenly gets stiff when the clip touches the pot.
ideas.form: A hand crank on the drum motor, a key in Jump in for force, clips to choose the load; a path traced film from the side with the crank and the pots in frame.

ideas.title: Lean on the lever down the dune
ideas.goal: The player rides the cart down the beach face with a hand on one lever: free, charging the pots, or a hard strap. Charge too hard and the leather belt slips and squeals; too little and the cart runs to the sea. Holding the line where the belt just grips puts the most charge back, a feel you get better at every run.
ideas.toward: Braking that charges the plates and the dune descent, both on the big goal's road, played by the player's own hand instead of a menu.
ideas.idea: The motor as a generator under load torque k*I, the belt's grip from the capstan law (T1/T2 = e^(mu theta)), the slope from the real crest. Someone watching sees the cart creep down a sandy slope, the belt jumping when the rider gets greedy.
ideas.form: A continuous control in the cart plugin; a film of two runs, one greedy, one held.
